text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zimbabwe Defence Minister Moven Mahachi said the government plans to spend Z$100 million on skills training for 11,000 men retrenched from the national army, and also to help them establish small businesses. The demobilised soldiers are now regarded a reserve defence force.
- Zimbabwe's cash-strapped state-owned national airline -- Air Zimbabwe -- has increased wages by 27.5 percent backdated to July to try to retain experienced staff among its nearly 2,000 employees.

- Zimbabwe's Wankie Colliery said its Z$500 million expansion programme was on track and the company was ready to increase coal output to service anticipated higher demand from Hwange Thermal Power Station.

- Three new listings are still expected on a booming Zimbabwe Stock Exchange (ZSE) in the coming few months, ZSE chief executive Tony Barfoot said told the Business Herald, reiterating a statement he made made weeks ago.
- Two Zimbabwean police officials died instantly and a third seriously injured when their truck crashed into a stationary light aircraft at Harare International Airport on Wednesday.
